did_you_know.text: Did you know? The men of Ephraim were angry with Gideon because he had not called them to join the war against Midian from the beginning, and they strongly argued with him.

Did you know? Gideon appeased the men of Ephraim by praising their achievements and saying that “Ephraim’s gleanings”—their later accomplishments—were better than “the harvest of Abiezer,” meaning the main achievement of his own men.
Did you know? After the battle, Gideon continued pursuing the enemy with his three hundred men, even though they were extremely exhausted.
Did you know? At the battle of Karkor, 120,000 men from the camp of the eastern peoples who were “armed with swords” fell, and only about 15,000 remained.
Did you know? A young man from Succoth wrote down for Gideon the names of the city’s officials and elders—seventy-seven men.
Did you know? Gideon learned that Zebah and Zalmunna had killed his brothers at Tabor; therefore, confronting them was personal for him as well as part of the war against Midian.
Did you know? The Israelites asked Gideon, his son, and his grandson to rule over them, but Gideon rejected the offer and declared, “The LORD will rule over you.”
Did you know? Gideon made an ephod from the gold collected as plunder and displayed it in Ophrah, but the ephod became a snare, leading Israel to worship it.
Did you know? After Midian was subdued, the land had peace for forty years during Gideon’s lifetime.
Did you know? Gideon had seventy sons, and he named the son born to him by his concubine in Shechem Abimelech.
